Lines.Line_01: Chapter 17

Lines.Line_12: my coat were all soaking wet before we had gone a
Lines.Line_13: hundred yards.

Lines.Line_15: to lie a little more evenly. All the same, we were afraid
Lines.Line_16: to breathe.

Lines.Line_18: strong rippling current running westward through the
Lines.Line_19: basin, and then southward and seaward down the straits
Lines.Line_20: by which we had entered in the morning. Even the
Lines.Line_21: ripples were a danger to our overloaded craft; but the

Lines.Line_23: course, and away from our proper landing-place behind

Lines.Line_18: then we all got aboard the other, and set out to go
Lines.Line_19: round by sea for North Inlet.
Lines.Line_20: This was a run of eight or nine miles. Silver,
Lines.Line_21: though he was almost killed already with fatigue,
Lines.Line_22: was set to an oar, like the rest of us, and we were
Lines.Line_23: soon skimming swiftly over a smooth sea. Soon we
Lines.Line_24: passed out of the straits and doubled the south-east
Lines.Line_25: corner of the island, round which, four days ago, we had
Lines.Line_26: towed the Hispaniola.
Lines.Line_27: As we passed the two-pointed hill, we could see the
Lines.Line_28: black mouth of Ben Gunn's cave, and a figure standing
Lines.Line_29: by it, leaning on a musket. It was the squire; and

Lesson_0283.Name: Lesson_0283

Lines.Line_01: we waved a handkerchief and gave him three cheers,
Lines.Line_02: in which the voice of Silver joined as heartily as any.
Lines.Line_03: Three miles farther, just inside the mouth of North
Lines.Line_04: Inlet, what should we meet but the Hispaniola, cruising
Lines.Line_05: by herself? The last flood had lifted her; and had
Lines.Line_06: there been much wind, or a strong tide current, as in
Lines.Line_07: the southern anchorage, we should never have found
Lines.Line_08: her more, or found her stranded beyond help. As it
Lines.Line_09: was, there was little amiss, beyond the wreck of the
Lines.Line_10: mainsail. Another anchor was got ready, and dropped
Lines.Line_11: in a fathom and a half of water. We all pulled round
Lines.Line_12: again to Rum Cove, the nearest point for Ben Gunn's
Lines.Line_13: treasure-house; and then Gray, single-handed, returned
Lines.Line_14: with the gig to the Hispaniola, where he was to pass
Lines.Line_15: the night on guard.
Lines.Line_16: A gentle slope ran up from the beach to the entrance
Lines.Line_17: of the cave. At the top, the squire met us. To me he
Lines.Line_18: was cordial and kind, saying nothing of my escapade,
Lines.Line_19: either in the way of blame or praise. At Silver's polite
Lines.Line_20: salute he somewhat flushed.
Lines.Line_21: "John Silver," he said, "you're a prodigious villain
Lines.Line_22: and impostor—a monstrous impostor, sir. I am told I
Lines.Line_23: am not to prosecute you. Well, then, I will not. But
Lines.Line_24: the dead men, sir, hang about your neck like mill-
Lines.Line_25: stones."
Lines.Line_26: "Thank you kindly, sir," replied Long John, again
Lines.Line_27: saluting.
Lines.Line_28: "I dare you to thank me!" cried the squire. "It
Lines.Line_29: is a gross dereliction of my duty. Stand back!"

Lesson_0284.Description: Part 6 - Chapter 33 - Page 283: The Fall of a Chieftain

Lines.Line_01: And thereupon we all entered the cave. It was a
Lines.Line_02: large, airy place, with a little spring and a pool of clear
Lines.Line_03: water, overhung with ferns. The floor was sand. Before
Lines.Line_04: a big fire lay Captain Smollett; and in a far corner,
Lines.Line_05: only duskily flickered over by the blaze, I beheld great
Lines.Line_06: heaps of coin and quadrilaterals built of bars of gold.
Lines.Line_07: That was Flint's treasure that we had come so far to
Lines.Line_08: seek, and that had cost already the lives of seventeen
Lines.Line_09: men from the Hispaniola. How many it had cost in
Lines.Line_10: the amassing, what blood and sorrow, what good ships
Lines.Line_11: scuttled on the deep, what brave men walking the plank
Lines.Line_12: blindfold, what shot of cannon, what shame and lies and
Lines.Line_13: cruelty, perhaps no man alive could tell. Yet there were
Lines.Line_14: still three upon that island—Silver, and old Morgan,
Lines.Line_15: and Ben Gunn—who had each taken his share in these
Lines.Line_16: crimes, as each had hoped in vain to share in the
Lines.Line_17: reward.
Lines.Line_18: "Come in, Jim," said the captain. "You're a good
Lines.Line_19: boy in your line, Jim; but I don't think you and me'll
Lines.Line_20: go to sea again. You're too much of the born favourite
Lines.Line_21: for me. Is that you, John Silver? What brings you
Lines.Line_22: here, man?"
Lines.Line_23: "Come back to my dooty, sir," returned Silver.
Lines.Line_24: "Ah!" said the captain; and that was all he
Lines.Line_25: said.
Lines.Line_26: What a supper I had of it that night, with all my
Lines.Line_27: friends around me; and what a meal it was, with Ben
Lines.Line_28: Gunn's salted goat, and some delicacies and a bottle of
Lines.Line_29: old wine from the Hispaniola. Never, I am sure, were

Lesson_0285.Name: Lesson_0285
Lesson_0285.Description: Part 6 - Chapter 33 - Page 284: The Fall of a Chieftain

Lines.Line_01: people gayer or happier. And there was Silver, sitting
Lines.Line_02: back almost out of the firelight, but eating heartily,
Lines.Line_03: prompt to spring forward when anything was wanted,
Lines.Line_04: even joining quietly in our laughter—the same bland,
Lines.Line_05: polite, obsequious seaman of the voyage out.

Lines.Line_01: Chapter 34
Lines.Line_02: And Last
Lines.Line_03: The next morning we fell early to work, for the
Lines.Line_04: transportation of this great mass of gold near a mile by
Lines.Line_05: land to the beach, and thence three miles by boat to the
Lines.Line_06: Hispaniola, was a considerable task for so small a number
Lines.Line_07: of workmen. The three fellows still abroad upon the
Lines.Line_08: Island did not greatly trouble us; a single sentry on
Lines.Line_09: the shoulder of the hill was sufficient to insure us
Lines.Line_10: against any sudden onslaught, and we thought, besides,
Lines.Line_11: they had had more than enough of fighting.
Lines.Line_12: Therefore the work was pushed on briskly. Gray
Lines.Line_13: and Ben Gunn came and went with the boat, while the
Lines.Line_14: rest during their absences, piled treasure on the beach.
Lines.Line_15: Two of the bars, slung in a rope's-end, made a good
Lines.Line_16: load for a grown man—one that he was glad to walk
Lines.Line_17: slowly with. For my part, as I was not much use at
Lines.Line_18: carrying, I was kept busy all day in the cave, packing
Lines.Line_19: the minted money into bread-bags.
Lines.Line_20: It was a strange collection, like Billy Bones's hoard
Lines.Line_21: for the diversity of coinage, but so much larger and so
Lines.Line_22: much more varied that I think I never had more
Lines.Line_23: pleasure than in sorting them. English, French,

Lines.Line_01: Spanish, Portuguese, Georges, and Louises, doubloons
Lines.Line_02: and double guineas and moidores and sequins, the
Lines.Line_03: pictures of all the kings of Europe for the last hundred
Lines.Line_04: years, strange Oriental pieces stamped with what looked
Lines.Line_05: like wisps of string or bits of spider's web, round pieces
Lines.Line_06: and square pieces, and pieces bored through the middle,
Lines.Line_07: as if to wear them round your neck—nearly every
Lines.Line_08: variety of money in the world must, I think, have found
Lines.Line_09: a place in that collection; and for number, I am sure
Lines.Line_10: they were like autumn leaves, so that my back ached
Lines.Line_11: with stooping and my fingers with sorting them out.
Lines.Line_12: Day after day this work went on; by every evening
Lines.Line_13: a fortune had been stowed aboard, but there was another
Lines.Line_14: fortune waiting for the morrow; and all this time we
Lines.Line_15: heard nothing of the three surviving mutineers.
Lines.Line_16: At last—I think it was on the third night—the
Lines.Line_17: doctor and I were strolling on the shoulder of the hill
Lines.Line_18: where it overlooks the lowlands of the isle, when, from
Lines.Line_19: out the thick darkness below, the wind brought us a
Lines.Line_20: noise between shrieking and singing. It was only a
Lines.Line_21: snatch that reached our ears, followed by the former
Lines.Line_22: silence.
Lines.Line_23: 'Heaven forgive them,' said the doctor; 'tis the
Lines.Line_24: mutineers!'
Lines.Line_25: 'All drunk, sir,' struck in the voice of Silver from
Lines.Line_26: behind us.
Lines.Line_27: Silver, I should say, was allowed his entire liberty,
Lines.Line_28: and, in spite of daily rebuffs, seemed to regard himself
Lines.Line_29: once more as quite a privileged and friendly dependant.

Lines.Line_01: Indeed, it was remarkable how well he bore these
Lines.Line_02: slights, and with what unwearying politeness he kept
Lines.Line_03: on trying to ingratiate himself with all. Yet, I think,
Lines.Line_04: none treated him better than a dog; unless it was Ben
Lines.Line_05: Gunn, who was still terribly afraid of his old quarter-
Lines.Line_06: master, or myself, who had really something to thank
Lines.Line_07: him for; although for that matter, I suppose, I had
Lines.Line_08: reason to think even worse of him than anybody else,
Lines.Line_09: for I had seen him meditating a fresh treachery upon
Lines.Line_10: the plateau. Accordingly, it was pretty gruffly that
Lines.Line_11: the doctor answered him.
Lines.Line_12: "Drunk or raving," said he.
Lines.Line_13: "Right you were, sir," replied Silver; "and
Lines.Line_14: precious little odds which, to you and me."
Lines.Line_15: "I suppose you would hardly ask me to call you
Lines.Line_16: a humane man," returned the doctor, with a sneer,
Lines.Line_17: "and so my feelings may surprise you, Master Silver.
Lines.Line_18: But if I were sore they were raving—as I am morally
Lines.Line_19: certain one, at least, of them is down with fever—I
Lines.Line_20: should leave this camp, and, at whatever risk to my own
Lines.Line_21: carcase, take them the assistance of my skill."
Lines.Line_22: "Ask your pardon, sir, you would be very wrong,"
Lines.Line_23: quoth Silver. "You would lose your precious life, and
Lines.Line_24: you may lay to that. I'm on your side now, hand and
Lines.Line_25: glove; and I shouldn't wish for to see the party weakened,
Lines.Line_26: let alone yourself, seeing as I know what I owes you.
Lines.Line_27: But these men down there, they couldn't keep their word
Lines.Line_28: —no, not supposing they wished to; and what's more,
Lines.Line_29: they couldn't believe as you could."

Lines.Line_01: "No," said the doctor. "You're the man to keep
Lines.Line_02: your word, we know that."
Lines.Line_03: Well, that was about the last news we had of the
Lines.Line_04: three pirates. Only once we heard a gunshot a great
Lines.Line_05: way off, and supposed them to be hunting. A council
Lines.Line_06: was held, and it was decided that we must desert them
Lines.Line_07: on the island—to the huge glee, I must say, of Ben
Lines.Line_08: Gunn, and with the strong approval of Gray. We left
Lines.Line_09: a good stock of powder and shot, the bulk of the salt
Lines.Line_10: goat, a few medicines, and some other necessaries, tools,
Lines.Line_11: clothing, a spare sail, a fathom or two of rope, and, by
Lines.Line_12: the particular desire of the doctor, a handsome present
Lines.Line_13: of tobacco.
Lines.Line_14: That was about our last doing on the island. Before
Lines.Line_15: that, we had got the treasure stowed, and had shipped
Lines.Line_16: enough water and the remainder of the goat meat, in
Lines.Line_17: case of any distress; and at last, one fine morning, we
Lines.Line_18: weighed anchor, which was about all that we could
Lines.Line_19: manage, and stood out of North Inlet, the same colours
Lines.Line_20: flying that the captain had flown and fought under at
Lines.Line_21: the palisade.
Lines.Line_22: The three fellows must have been watching us closer
Lines.Line_23: than we thought for, as we soon had proved. For,
Lines.Line_24: coming through the narrows, we had to lie very near the
Lines.Line_25: southern point, and there we saw all three of them
Lines.Line_26: kneeling together on a spit of sand, with their arms
Lines.Line_27: raised in supplication. It went to all our hearts, I
Lines.Line_28: think, to leave them in that wretched state; but we
Lines.Line_29: could not risk another mutiny; and to take them home

Lines.Line_01: for the gibbet would have been a cruel sort of kindness.
Lines.Line_02: The doctor hailed them and told them of the stores we
Lines.Line_03: had left, and where they were to find them. But they
Lines.Line_04: continued to call us by name, and appeal to us, for God's
Lines.Line_05: sake, to be merciful, and not leave them to die in such a
Lines.Line_06: place.
Lines.Line_07: At last, seeing the ship still bore on her course, and
Lines.Line_08: was now swiftly drawing out of earshot, one of them—
Lines.Line_09: I know not which it was—leapt to his feet with a hoarse
Lines.Line_10: cry, whipped his musket to his shoulder, and sent a shot
Lines.Line_11: whistling over Silver's head and through the main-sail.
Lines.Line_12: After that, we kept under cover of the bulwarks, and
Lines.Line_13: when next I looked out they had disappeared from the
Lines.Line_14: spit, and the spit itself had almost melted out of sight
Lines.Line_15: in the growing distance. That was, at least, the end of
Lines.Line_16: that; and before noon, to my inexpressible joy, the
Lines.Line_17: highest rock of Treasure Island had sunk into the blue
Lines.Line_18: round of sea.
Lines.Line_19: We were so short of men, that every one on board
Lines.Line_20: had to bear a hand—only the captain lying on a mattress
Lines.Line_21: in the stern and giving his orders; for, though greatly
Lines.Line_22: recovered he was still in want of quiet. We laid her
Lines.Line_23: head for the nearest port in Spanish America, for we
Lines.Line_24: could not risk the voyage home without fresh hands;
Lines.Line_25: and as it was, what with baffling winds and a couple of
Lines.Line_26: fresh gales, we were all worn out before we reached it.
Lines.Line_27: It was just at sundown when we cast anchor in a
Lines.Line_28: most beautiful land-locked gulf, and were immediately
Lines.Line_29: surrounded by shore boats full of negroes, and Mexican

Lines.Line_01: Indians, and half-bloods, selling fruits and vegetables,
Lines.Line_02: and, offering to dive for bits of money. The sight of
Lines.Line_03: so many good-humoured faces (especially the blacks),
Lines.Line_04: the taste of the tropical fruits, and above all, the
Lines.Line_05: lights that began to shine in the town, made a most
Lines.Line_06: charming contrast to our dark and bloody sojourn on
Lines.Line_07: the island; and the doctor and the squire, taking me
Lines.Line_08: along with them, went ashore to pass the early part of
Lines.Line_09: the night. Here they met the captain of an English man-
Lines.Line_10: of-war, fell in talk with him, went on board his ship,
Lines.Line_11: and, in short, had so agreeable a time, that day was
Lines.Line_12: breaking when we came alongside the Hispaniola.
Lines.Line_13: Ben Gunn was on deck alone, and, as soon as we
Lines.Line_14: came on board, he began, with wonderful contortions,
Lines.Line_15: to make us a confession. Silver was gone. The
Lines.Line_16: maroon had connived at his escape in a shore boat
Lines.Line_17: some hours ago, and he now assured us he had only
Lines.Line_18: done so to preserve our lives, which would certainly
Lines.Line_19: have been forfeit if "that man with the one leg had
Lines.Line_20: stayed aboard."
Lines.Line_21: But this was not all. The sea-cook
Lines.Line_22: had not gone empty handed. He had cut through a
Lines.Line_23: bulkhead unobserved, and had removed one of the sacks
Lines.Line_24: of coin, worth, perhaps, three or four hundred guineas,
Lines.Line_25: to help him on his further wanderings.
Lines.Line_26: I think we were all pleased to be so cheaply quit of
Lines.Line_27: him.
Lines.Line_28: Well, to make a long story short, we got a few
Lines.Line_29: hands on board, made a good cruise home, and the
Lines.Line_30: Hispaniola reached Bristol just as Mr. Blandly was

Lines.Line_01: beginning to think of fitting out her consort. Five
Lines.Line_02: men only of those who had sailed returned with her.
Lines.Line_03: "Drink and the devil had done for the rest," with a
Lines.Line_04: vengeance; although, to be sure, we were not quite
Lines.Line_05: in so bad a case as that other ship they sang about:
Lines.Line_06: "With one man of her crew alive,
Lines.Line_07: What put to sea with seventy-five."
Lines.Line_08: All of us had an ample share of the treasure, and
Lines.Line_09: used it wisely or foolishly, according to our natures.
Lines.Line_10: Captain Smollett is now retired from the sea. Gray
Lines.Line_11: not only saved his money, but, being suddenly smit
Lines.Line_12: with the desire to rise, also studied his profession; and
Lines.Line_13: he is now mate and part owner of a fine full-rigged
Lines.Line_14: ship; married besides, and the father of a family. As
Lines.Line_15: for Ben Gunn, he got a thousand pounds, which he
Lines.Line_16: spent or lost in three weeks, or, to be more exact, in
Lines.Line_17: nineteen days, for he was back begging on the twentieth.
Lines.Line_18: Then he was given a lodge to keep, exactly as he had
Lines.Line_19: feared upon the island; and he still lives, a great
Lines.Line_20: favourite, though something of a butt, with the country
Lines.Line_21: boys, and a notable singer in church on Sundays and
Lines.Line_22: saints' days.
Lines.Line_23: Of Silver we have heard no more. That formidable
Lines.Line_24: seafaring man with one leg has at last gone clean out of
Lines.Line_25: my life; but I daresay he met his old negress, and per-
Lines.Line_26: haps still lives in comfort with her and Captain Flint.
Lines.Line_27: It is to be hoped so, I suppose, for his chances of com-
Lines.Line_28: fort in another world are very small.

Lines.Line_01: The bar silver and the arms still lie, for all that I
Lines.Line_02: know, where Flint buried them; and certainly they shall
Lines.Line_03: lie there for me. Oxen and wain-ropes would not
Lines.Line_04: bring me back again to that accursed island; and the
Lines.Line_05: worst dreams that ever I have are when I hear the
Lines.Line_06: surf booming about its coasts, or start upright in bed,
Lines.Line_07: with the sharp voice of Captain Flint still ringing in
Lines.Line_08: my ears:
Lines.Line_09: "Pieces of eight!
Lines.Line_10: pieces of eight!"
